correctness.rationale: For finite connected simple bipartite unweighted graph under p>q≥2 side degree caps, C(s)=2(I+sL)^{-1}−I, and the inverse M-matrix is strictly positive off diagonal. The sole obstruction is a resolvent diagonal below 1/2. Lifting nonnegative closed-walk weights to the universal cover gives a lower bound; adding missing branches to form the (p,q)-biregular tree increases the Laplacian in Loewner order, further lowers its root resolvent. The two-type cavity functions a=1/[t+p−(p−1)b], b=1/[t+q−(q−1)a] with t=1/s retain parent degrees correctly. Their physical root has 0<a<b<1 and the p-side diagonal is the smaller, monotone return. Substituting R_p=1/2 gives b=1−t/p, a=p/[p+(2p−1)t] and D+B t−(2p−1)t²=0 (B=2p²−2pq−2p+q,D=p(2pq−p−q)>0), with exactly one positive root t<p. σ=1/t therefore guarantees positivity for all s≤σ; finite radius balls with ordinary internal-edge Laplacians converge to the limiting tree return, giving a finite negative diagonal for every s>σ. Completing the q-side less than p also proves strict gain over σ_p=(2p−1)/(2p(p−1)). Half-step s=h/2, s=0, caps not exact degrees, and absence of finite extremal equality are handled. Independently checked cavity/quadratic algebra and representative finite graph inverses; proof supplies all graphs.

value.rationale: Separate degree ceilings for the two parts of bipartite diffusion/transport graphs are meaningful structural information. The sharp two-parameter algebraic step improves on the best p-only bound without eigensolving individual graphs; its finite-ball extremizers prove that the improvement is genuinely optimal over all finite topologies. A sharp uniform frontier over an infinite natural family, even with modest numeric gain, is a structural mathematical contribution.

limitations: Unnormalized, unit-conductance, simple undirected connected bipartite finite graphs, p>q≥2, half-step s=h/2 only; no variable conductances, directed graphs or error/convergence assertions.
